questionText: A ticket counter holds only ₹100, ₹20 and ₹10 notes. It has twice as many ₹20 notes as ₹100 notes and three times as many ₹10 notes as ₹100 notes. The notes come to ₹3,060 in all. How many notes does the counter hold?
solution:
Rule: call the smallest group one share and write every other group in shares.
Set up the shares: ₹100 notes = 1 share
₹20 notes = 2 shares
₹10 notes = 3 shares
Value carried by one share: ₹100 × 1 = ₹100
₹20 × 2 = ₹40
₹10 × 3 = ₹30
One share is worth ₹100 + ₹40 + ₹30 = ₹170
Find the size of a share: ₹3, 060 ÷ ₹170 = 18
Count the notes: ₹100 notes = 18
₹20 notes = 2 × 18 = 36
₹10 notes = 3 × 18 = 54
Total = 18 + 36 + 54 = 108
Answer: 108
conceptTested: Proportional distribution of denominations and calculating total items in a collection based on a given monetary value.

questionText: The symbol $\oplus$ follows one rule throughout: $9 \oplus 5 = 56$, $12 \oplus 7 = 95$ and $10 \oplus 6 = 64$. What is the value of $(15 \oplus 8) - (11 \oplus 9)$?
solution:
Rule: try the worked examples against the sum, the difference and the product before reaching for anything longer.
Read the examples: 9 × 5 = 45, so the rule is not the product.
9² = 81 and 5² = 25, and 81 - 25 = 56
12² - 7² = 144 - 49 = 95
10² - 6² = 100 - 36 = 64

So $a \oplus b = a^2 - b^2$.

The first bracket: $15 \oplus 8 = 225 - 64 = 161$
The second bracket: $11 \oplus 9 = 121 - 81 = 40$
Subtract, as the question asks: $161 - 40 = 121$
Answer: 121
conceptTested: Mathematical operation based on algebraic identity $a^2 - b^2$ applied to symbolic operators.

questionText: Four interns - Nandan, Ila, Tejas and Ruhi - sit in a row facing north, and each is posted to a different city: Bhuj, Kota, Salem or Thane. Ila sits at the extreme right end. Nandan sits second to the right of Ruhi. The intern posted to Bhuj sits immediately to the right of the one posted to Kota. Ila is posted to Thane. Nandan is not posted to Bhuj. To which city is Tejas posted?
solution:
The convention: All four face north, so each intern’s left and right run the same way as the page’s.
Fix the four seats: Ila takes the extreme right, seat 4.

Nandan sits two seats to Ruhi’s right, and of the seats left only 1 and 3 stand two apart.

So Ruhi is 1 and Nandan is 3.

Tejas takes the seat left over, 2.

The row, left to right: Ruhi, Tejas, Nandan, Ila
Post the cities: Ila at seat 4 has Thane.

Kota must sit immediately left of Bhuj, so that pair is seats 1 - 2 or seats 2 - 3.

Were it 2 - 3, Nandan at seat 3 would hold Bhuj, which he does not.

So Kota is seat 1 and Bhuj is seat 2, and Salem is left for seat 3.

The matching: • Ruhi - Kota
• Tejas - Bhuj
• Nandan - Salem
• Ila - Thane
Answer: Bhuj
conceptTested: Deduction of linear positions based on relative directional clues and attribute matching.

questionText: In a certain code language, 'PLANET' is coded as 68 and 'ORBIT' is coded as 64. How will 'COMET' be coded in that same code language?
solution:
Rule: add the alphabet positions of the letters and compare with the code.
Test PLANET: P = 16, L = 12, A = 1, N = 14, E = 5, T = 20
16 + 12 + 1 + 14 + 5 + 20 = 68
Test ORBIT: O = 15, R = 18, B = 2, I = 9, T = 20
15 + 18 + 2 + 9 + 20 = 64

Both codes are plain position sums.

Now COMET: C = 3, O = 15, M = 13, E = 5, T = 20
3 + 15 = 18
18 + 13 = 31
31 + 5 = 36
36 + 20 = 56
Answer: 56
conceptTested: Forward alphabetical position summation code for words.

questionText:
Which two signs and which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

$12 \div 6 + 3 \times 36 - 2 = 28$
solution:
Rule: swap the two signs first, then the two numbers, and solve by BODMAS.
The equation as printed: $12 \div 6 + 3 \times 36 - 2 = 2 + 108 - 2 = 108$, not 28.
Interchange $+$ and $\times$: Every $+$ becomes $\times$ and every $\times$ becomes $+$: $12 \div 6 \times 3 + 36 - 2$
Now interchange 12 and 36: $36 \div 6 \times 3 + 12 - 2$

$36 \div 6 = 6$

$6 \times 3 = 18$

$18 + 12 - 2 = 28$

This is the value the question asks for.
conceptTested: BODMAS rule combined with simultaneous interchange of mathematical signs and numbers to balance an equation.

questionText: For a concave mirror, an object is placed at $u = -15\text{ cm}$ and the focal length is $f = -10\text{ cm}$. Find the image distance $v$.
solution:
Answer: Option (a) - -30 cm

By the mirror formula $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$, we get $\frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{u} = -\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{15} = -\frac{1}{30}$, so $v = -30\text{ cm}$ - a real, inverted, enlarged image 30 cm in front of the mirror.

Revision note - mirror formula and magnification

The mirror formula is $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$, and the radius of curvature $R = 2f$.

Under the Cartesian sign convention distances are measured from the pole, with the incident ray direction taken as positive.

For a concave mirror $f$ is negative; for a convex mirror $f$ is positive.

Magnification $m = -\frac{v}{u} = \frac{h'}{h}$. A negative $m$ means a real, inverted image; a positive $m$ means a virtual, erect image.
conceptTested: Mirror formula $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$ and Cartesian sign conventions for concave mirrors.

Warren Hastings was Governor of Bengal from 1772 and became the first Governor - General of Bengal in 1774 under the Regulating Act of 1773.

Awadh was the chief buffer state, under the Treaty of Benaras, 1773.

questionText: Which of the following statements about the human heart and double circulation is correct?

options.A: The right ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta.
options.B: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the left atrium.
options.C: The pulmonary vein carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
options.D: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body.
options.a: The right ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta.
options.b: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the left atrium.
options.c: The pulmonary vein carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
options.d: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body.

solution:
Answer: Option (d) - The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body.

The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the left atrium and pumps it into the aorta for the whole body. Its wall is the thickest of the four chambers.

Revision note - the human heart and double circulation

The human heart has four chambers: two atria above and two ventricles below.

Deoxygenated blood from the body reaches the right atrium through the superior and inferior vena cava.

From the right ventricle it goes to the lungs through the pulmonary artery - the only artery carrying deoxygenated blood.

questionText: The perimeter of a rhombus is $100\text{ cm}$. If its longer diagonal measures $40\text{ cm}$, what is the area enclosed by the rhombus?
solution: All four sides of a rhombus are equal, so side = $100 \div 4 = 25\text{ cm}$. Half of the given diagonal = $40 \div 2 = 20\text{ cm}$. The half of the other diagonal is given by $\sqrt{25^2 - 20^2} = \sqrt{625 - 400} = \sqrt{225} = 15\text{ cm}$. So the other diagonal = $2 \times 15 = 30\text{ cm}$. Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{product of diagonals} = \frac{1}{2} \times 40 \times 30 = 600\text{ cm}^2$.
conceptTested: Relationship between side, perimeter, and diagonals of a rhombus: $d_2 = 2\sqrt{a^2 - (d_1/2)^2}$ and Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times d_1 \times d_2$.

questionText: At the close of the day a stores clerk at a district supply depot empties the counter cash box and finds that the whole of the day's collection is made up of ₹500 notes and ₹200 notes, with no other denomination and no coins at all. He counts $42$ notes in the box, and the day book shows that the collection came to ₹$15,600$. The audit clerk now wants the two kinds entered on separate lines. How many ₹$200$ notes are there in the box?
solution: Let the number of ₹$500$ notes be $n$. Then the ₹$200$ notes number $42 - n$. Build the money equation: $500n + 200(42 - n) = 15,600$. Opening the bracket: $500n + 8,400 - 200n = 15,600 \Rightarrow 300n = 7,200 \Rightarrow n = 24$ notes of ₹$500$. Therefore, the ₹$200$ notes = $42 - 24 = 18$ notes.
conceptTested: Solving linear simultaneous equations derived from total value and total count of denomination notes.

questionText: The public health wing of a municipal body has bought a cylindrical road roller for a newly laid colony road. The drum of the roller is $2\text{ metres}$ long and its diameter is $1.4\text{ metres}$, and only the curved surface of the drum ever touches the road. On the first morning the operator drives the roller from one end of the stretch to the other and the drum makes $750$ complete revolutions. Find the area of road levelled in that single run. (Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
solution: Radius $r = \frac{1.4}{2} = 0.7\text{ m}$. Curved surface area covered in one revolution = $2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 0.7 \times 2 = 8.8\text{ m}^2$. Total area covered in $750$ revolutions = $8.8 \times 750 = 6,600\text{ m}^2$.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: Two inlet pipes can fill an empty tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe at the bottom can empty the full tank in 20 hours. All three are opened together when the tank is empty. In how many hours will the tank be filled?
solution:
Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of 12, 15, and 20, which is $60$ units.

First inlet 1 - hour work = $60 \div 12 = 5$ units/houRs. econd inlet 1 - hour work = $60 \div 15 = 4$ units/hour
Outlet 1 - hour work (emptying) = $60 \div 20 = 3$ units/hour

Net work done per hour when all three pipes are opened together = $5 + 4 - 3 = 6$ units/hour.

Total time required to fill the tank = $\frac{60}{6} = 10$ hours.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: A sum of money becomes three times itself in 12 years at simple interest. In how many years will the same sum become five times itself at the same rate?
solution:
Let the principal be $P$.

If the amount becomes $3P$ in 12 years, the simple interest earned is $3P - P = 2P$.

Thus, an interest of $2P$ takes 12 years, which means an interest of $P$ takes $\frac{12}{2} = 6$ years.

To become 5 times itself, the amount must be $5P$, so the required interest is $5P - P = 4P$.

Time required to earn $4P$ interest = $4 \times 6 = 24$ years.
conceptTested: Simple interest is directly proportional to time for a constant principal and rate of interest.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: If $2 \cos^2\theta + 3 \sin \theta = 3$ and $\theta$ is an acute angle, find the value of $\theta$.
solution:
We are given: $$2 \cos^2\theta + 3 \sin \theta = 3$$
Substitute $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$: $$2(1 - \sin^2\theta) + 3 \sin \theta = 3$$

$$2 - 2 \sin^2\theta + 3 \sin \theta = 3$$

$$2 \sin^2\theta - 3 \sin \theta + 1 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic equation: $$(2 \sin \theta - 1)(\sin \theta - 1) = 0$$
This gives: $$\sin \theta = \frac{1}{2} \quad \text{or} \quad \sin \theta = 1$$

Since $\theta$ is an acute angle, $\sin \theta = 1$ gives $\theta = 90^\circ$ (which is not strictly acute or leads to the boundary condition, whereas $\sin \theta = \frac{1}{2}$ gives $\theta = 30^\circ$). Therefore, $\theta = 30^\circ$.
conceptTested: Solving trigonometric quadratic equations using $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: In a quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle ABC = 90^\circ$, $AB = 6\text{ cm}$, $BC = 8\text{ cm}$, $CD = 17\text{ cm}$ and $DA = 21\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the quadrilateral.
solution:
Join diagonal $AC$. In right - angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ at $B$: $$AC = \sqrt{AB^2 + BC^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ cm}$$

Area of $\triangle ABC$ = $\frac{1}{2} \times AB \times BC = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24\text{ cm}^2$.

For $\triangle ACD$, the sides are $a = 10\text{ cm}$, $b = 17\text{ cm}$, and $c = 21\text{ cm}$.

Semi - perimeter $s = \frac{10 + 17 + 21}{2} = 24$.

Using Heron's formula: $$\text{Area of } \triangle ACD = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{24 \times (24-10) \times (24-17) \times (24-21)}$$

$$= \sqrt{24 \times 14 \times 7 \times 3} = \sqrt{7056} = 84\text{ cm}^2$$

Total area of quadrilateral $ABCD$ = $\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) + \text{Area}(\triangle ACD) = 24 + 84 = 108\text{ cm}^2$.
conceptTested: Application of Pythagoras theorem and Heron's formula for finding the area of a non-standard quadrilateral.

questionText: The table shows the monthly sales (in units) of four electronic items across four months. Find the month with the second lowest average sales.
solution:
Summing the sales for each month across the 4 items: - **June:** $180 + 140 + 120 + 60 = 500$ - **July:** $210 + 150 + 132 + 60 = 552$ - **August:** $165 + 130 + 118 + 71 = 484$ - **September:** $195 + 145 + 108 + 80 = 528$
Calculating the average for each month (divide by 4 items): - June average = $500 \div 4 = 125$ - July average = $552 \div 4 = 138$ - August average = $484 \div 4 = 121$ - September average = $528 \div 4 = 132$
Arranging the averages in ascending order: $$121 (August) < 125 (June) < 132 (September) < 138 (July)$$

Thus, the lowest average is August, and the **second lowest** average is **June**.
conceptTested: Finding averages from tabular data and identifying specific rank values.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: A storm snaps a vertical electric pole at a point above the ground. The broken part does not come away; its top rests on the ground 9 metres from the foot of the pole and makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the ground. Find the height of the pole before the storm.
solution:
Name the two pieces.

The stump still standing is the upright leg and the broken part is the slanting piece that meets the ground at $30^\circ$.

The standing stump: $\tan 30^\circ = \text{stump} \div 9$

$\text{stump} = 9 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = 3\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$

The broken part: $\cos 30^\circ = 9 \div \text{broken part}$

$\text{broken part} = 9 \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$

The pole before the storm: $\text{Height} = \text{stump} + \text{broken part} = 3\sqrt{3} + 6\sqrt{3} = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: Simplify: $(\sec θ - \cos θ)(\csc θ - \sin θ)(\tan θ + \cot θ)$
solution:
Rule: write every term in $\sin θ$ and $\cos θ$ before multiplying anything.
First bracket: $\sec θ - \cos θ = \frac{1}{\cos θ} - \cos θ = \frac{1 - \cos^2 θ}{\cos θ} = \frac{\sin^2 θ}{\cos θ}$
Second bracket: $\csc θ - \sin θ = \frac{1}{\sin θ} - \sin θ = \frac{1 - \sin^2 θ}{\sin θ} = \frac{\cos^2 θ}{\sin θ}$
Third bracket: $\tan θ + \cot θ = \frac{\sin θ}{\cos θ} + \frac{\cos θ}{\sin θ} = \frac{\sin^2 θ + \cos^2 θ}{\sin θ \cos θ} = \frac{1}{\sin θ \cos θ}$
Multiply the first two: $\left(\frac{\sin^2 θ}{\cos θ}\right) \times \left(\frac{\cos^2 θ}{\sin θ}\right) = \sin θ \cos θ$
Bring in the third: $\sin θ \cos θ \times \frac{1}{\sin θ \cos θ} = 1$
conceptTested: Fundamental trigonometric identities: $\sec θ - \cos θ = \frac{\sin^2 θ}{\cos θ}$, $\csc θ - \sin θ = \frac{\cos^2 θ}{\sin θ}$, and $\tan θ + \cot θ = \frac{1}{\sin θ \cos θ}$

questionText: Find the coordinates of the circumcentre of a triangle whose vertices are $(1, 1)$, $(7, 1)$ and $(3, 5)$.
solution:
Let the circumcentre be $P(x, y)$, with $A(1, 1)$, $B(7, 1)$, $C(3, 5)$.

AB is horizontal, so its perpendicular bisector is the vertical line: $x = \frac{1 + 7}{2} = 4$

Now use $PA = PC$ with $x = 4$: $(4 - 1)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = (4 - 3)^2 + (y - 5)^2$

$9 + y^2 - 2y + 1 = 1 + y^2 - 10y + 25$

$10 - 2y = 26 - 10y$

$8y = 16 \implies y = 2$

Circumcentre = $(4, 2)$

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: Find the minimum value of the expression $2x^2 - 8x + 15$.
solution:
Rule - where a quadratic is smallest. Write it as a perfect square plus a number. A square can never fall below zero, so that number left over is the least value.

Pull the 2 out of the first two terms: $2x^2 - 8x + 15 = 2(x^2 - 4x) + 15$
Complete the square inside: $x^2 - 4x = (x - 2)^2 - 4$

$= 2[(x - 2)^2 - 4] + 15$

$= 2(x - 2)^2 - 8 + 15$

$= 2(x - 2)^2 + 7$

Read the least value off: $(x - 2)^2$ is smallest at $x = 2$, where it becomes 0, leaving only the 7.
Minimum value = 7
conceptTested: Completing the square method to find the minimum value of a quadratic expression $ax^2 + bx + c$

questionText: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a point lying on the circle. If AC = 16 cm and BC = 12 cm, find the radius of the circle.
solution:
Rule - the angle in a semicircle. An angle drawn on a diameter from any point of the circle is a right angle. So $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$. That makes AB the hypotenuse.

$AB = \sqrt{16^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{256 + 144} = \sqrt{400} = 20\text{ cm}$

AB is the diameter, not the radius.

$\text{Radius} = 20 \div 2 = 10\text{ cm}$

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: The present ages of Ramesh and his younger sister are in the ratio $7 : 4$. Eight years from now the ratio of their ages will be $3 : 2$. Find Ramesh's present age.
solution:
Write the present ages as parts.

Ramesh = $7x$ and his sister = $4x$

Add 8 years to each of them.

$(7x + 8) : (4x + 8) = 3 : 2$

Cross - multiply.

$2(7x + 8) = 3(4x + 8)$

$14x + 16 = 12x + 24$

Solve for $x$.

$2x = 8$

$x = 4$

Ramesh's present age = $7 \times 4 = 28$ years.
conceptTested: Linear equations based on ratio changes over a time period

questionText: The average age of the 11 members of a colony welfare committee is 42 years. One more member joins the committee and the average age falls by 1.5 years. Find the age of the member who joined.
solution:
Total age before he joined = $11 \times 42 = 462$ years.
The new average = $42 - 1.5 = 40.5$ years.
Total age after he joined (12 members) = $12 \times 40.5 = 486$ years.
The newcomer's age = $486 - 462 = 24$ years.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questionText: When 85, 190 and 330 are each divided by the same number, the remainder is the same every time. Find the greatest such number.
solution:
Rule - the same remainder every time.

Take the differences: $190 - 85 = 105$

$330 - 190 = 140$

$330 - 85 = 245$

The divisor must divide all three differences. So the greatest one is the HCF of 105, 140 and 245.

$105 = 3 \times 5 \times 7$

$140 = 2 \times 2 \times 5 \times 7$

$245 = 5 \times 7 \times 7$

Common part = $5 \times 7 = 35$.
conceptTested: Greatest number that leaves the same remainder when dividing multiple given numbers is the HCF of their pairwise differences

Meaning: nepotism = favouring one's own relatives in appointments (भाई-भतीजावाद). - Cronyism = favouring close friends. - Patronage = support given by a powerful person. - Favouritism = general partiality without necessarily involving relatives.

Only nepotism specifies the favouring of blood relatives.
